subject: Controlling for the influence of independent variables in MG-SEM

messages.author: ec12e510d7b112ad
messages.subject: Controlling for the influence of independent variables in MG-SEM
parts:
Hello lavaan-group, 
I know that this might not be a lavaan specific question. Anyway, I have the following problem: I have four latent variables which are compared across two different groups. I´m aware of how it works and the issue of measurement invariance. There is one single-item "pseudo factor" Doku which is indeed measured without any error (see Brown 2006, Kline 2016). I want to control for the influence of the variable "Doku" (just like in a "classical" ANCOVA) while testing for group differences on the dependent variables. Is it correct to regress them onto the variable "Doku"? Compared to a model without the regression, the means are adjusted. Of course, lavaan will estimated the regression coefficients freely across the groups. Is that meaningful? I do have a theoretical justification, but as far as I know this is not done in ANCOVA, right? I think that covariates in ANCOVA should actually be equal across groups...  Any help is greatly appreciated! 


Thanks
Tobias 



arg.model.4fak.5Items.MG<-'
int=~ i1.03+i1.09+i1.16+i1.18+i1.21
exp=~ i6.05+i6.08+i6.11+i6.15+i6.16
mu=~  i7b.22+i7b.08+i7b.16+i7b.17+i7b.04
evi=~ i8.05+i8.09+i8.11+i8.14+i8.18
i1.18~~i1.21
i1.03~~i1.16
i6.08~~i6.15
i7b.22~~i7b.04

#single-item indicator
Doku=~Score.Doku
Score.Doku~~0*Score.Doku

#regression
int+mu+evi~Doku
'

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Controlling for the influence of independent variables in MG-SEM
parts: I want to control for the influence of the variable "Doku" (just like in a "classical" ANCOVA) while testing for group differences on the dependent variables. Is it correct to regress them onto the variable "Doku"? Compared to a model without the regression, the means are adjusted. Of course, lavaan will estimated the regression coefficients freely across the groups. Is that meaningful? I do have a theoretical justification, but as far as I know this is not done in ANCOVA, right? I think that covariates in ANCOVA should actually be equal across groups...

Yes, you are referring to the "assumption" of homogeneous slopes/hyperplanes in ANCOVA.  In order to test group-differences in adjusted means (or equivalently, group-differences in intercepts in a regression model), the distance between 2 groups' regression lines need to be constant across all levels of the covariate (Doku).  If there is an interaction between Doku and Group, then the lines are not parallel, so group differences are larger at some levels of Doku than at other levels of Doku.  In this case, there is no single valid test of difference in adjusted means or intercepts; instead, you would probe the interaction by testing group-mean differences at multiple meaningful levels of Doku (e.g., the observed minimum, maximum, and median, or the Mean + / - SD, or any levels of Doku that are substantively interesting "subpopulations" to compare).  You do this by centering Doku at each of the chosen levels and running your model(s) again, so that "Doku == 0" represents that centered value.  This works because in the presence of an interaction, the test of a difference in group intercepts (i.e., the effect of Group) is conditional on the moderator (Doku) being held constant at zero.

In the context of a multiple-group CFA/MIMIC model, Group implicitly interacts with every predictor (in your case, Doku and latent factors) because slopes are freely estimated across groups.  In fact, the test of metric (or "weak") invariance is a test of the interaction between Group and the latent factor(s) on the outcomes/indicators.  I will also point out that because you are interested in testing for group-differences in latent intercepts, you need to assume not only that the latent factors are measured invariably across groups, but also that the latent factors are measured invariably across levels of Doku.  If Doku is a continuous variable, you can test invariance using the MIMIC method.  Basically, fit a series of configural-invariance models (i.e., free estimates across groups) in which Doku predicts not only the latent factors but also one indicator per factor, and test whether the effect of Doku on each indicator is zero after controlling for the effect of the latent factor.  You will have to test all indicators, so use a Bonferroni-adjusted alpha level for the number of indicators you test.  If any are significant in either group, include those effects in your configural model when you start to test invariance across groups.  For a valid test of scalar (or "strong") invariance, you will first need to test whether the effects of Doku on any indicators differ across groups (i.e., whether Group and Doku interact in their effects on indicators -- this is testing the assumption of homogenous slopes across groups for the measurement model).  It doesn't matter whether you test the equality of "indicator ~ Doku" effects before or after testing metric invariance, but I would do them in separate steps because they are distinct null hypotheses.  If any Doku effects on indicators exist, and they cannot be constrained across groups, then you have to test partial scalar invariance across groups (i.e., don't constrain intercepts across groups for those indicators).

Back to your original question -- Assuming you have at least partial measurement invariance with respect to Group and to Doku, then you need to test whether the effects of Doku on latent factors are equal across groups.  If none differ, then there is no evidence of an interaction, so you can finally test group-differences in latent intercepts while controlling for Doku (same as testing group-differences in adjusted means in ANCOVA).  However, if any effects of Doku on latent variables differ across groups, then you would need to probe the Group-Doku interaction by testing group-mean differences at some meaningful levels of Doku (use centering, as described in the first paragraph).

Good luck,

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Controlling for the influence of independent variables in MG-SEM
parts: Do I estimate two models with the arguments group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts") and group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "regression") and compare if the latter fits significantly worse - if so I do assume that the effect of Doku is not equal across groups?

Yes, assuming those are the only regression parameters in your model (besides "loadings").  But it might be safer to explicitly label the regression parameters you want to constrain (e.g., 'int ~ c(beta1, beta1)*Doku'), assigning different labels to each group in the unconstrained model (e.g., 'int ~ c(beta1, beta2)*Doku').
This is done by evaluating the mean structure of  the latter model group.equal=c("loadings", "intercepts", "regressions") , right?

Yes, but again, I would recommend labeling regression parameters and latent intercepts in the syntax so you know exactly what you are constraining.  The "intercepts" in the group.equal argument refer only to observed indicators.  Latent variables would be "means", but that is confusing because your latent variables will be endogenous, so the means aren't actually estimated.  You can specify and label the latent intercepts by regressing the latent factors on 1 (e.g.,  'int ~ c(int.intercept1, int.intercept2)*1').
